items.title: Hackers abuse Google ads for GoDaddy ManageWP login phishing
items.description: A phishing campaign delivered through Google sponsored search results is targeting credentials for ManageWP, GoDaddy's platform for managing fleets of WordPress websites. [...]

items.title: Yet Another Way to Bypass Google Chrome's Encryption Protection
items.description: Authors of the VoidStealer Trojan uncovered a way to get around Google's App-Bound Encryption (ABE), opening the door to infostealers.

items.title: Instructure Breach Exposes Schools' Vendor Dependence
items.description: ShinyHunters' attack on Instructure, which owns the widely used Canvas learning management system (LMS), carries big questions about the trust educational institutions put into their vendors.

items.title: Mirai-Based xlabs_v1 Botnet Exploits ADB to Hijack IoT Devices for DDoS Attacks
items.description: Cybersecurity researchers have exposed a new Mirai-derived botnet that self-identifies as xlabs_v1 and targets internet-exposed devices running Android Debug Bridge (ADB) to enlist them in a network capable of carrying out distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. items.title: Critical vm2 sandbox bug lets attackers execute code on hosts
items.description: A critical vulnerability in the popular Node.js sandboxing library vm2 allows escaping the sandbox and executing arbitrary code on the host system. [...]

items.title: CloudZ RAT Abuses Microsoft Phone Link to Steal SMS OTPs and Mobile Notifications
items.description: A newly discovered threat is turning a built-in Microsoft feature into a powerful spying tool. Security researchers have found a remote access tool called CloudZ that works alongside a custom plugin named Pheno to silently intercept SMS messages and one-time passwords (OTPs) from mobile phones, all without ever touching the phone itself. items.title: QLNX Targets Developers With Credential Theft Designed for Supply Chain Compromise
items.description: A new and previously undocumented Linux threat has emerged, targeting software developers in a way that could put entire supply chains at risk. Named Quasar Linux, or QLNX, this malware operates as a full-featured remote access trojan built specifically for Linux systems.
